notes: THE soundness case, and the reason this port deviates from sqlx. PostgreSQL 16 replans this as `Hash Join / Join Type: Right` with the (b JOIN c) subtree as the OUTER child and `a` as the INNER child. sqlx's rule marks the child whose Parent Relationship is "Inner" -- which under a Right join is the PRESERVED side -- so it would call a.id nullable (harmless) and b.id/c.id NOT NULL (unsound). Verified against live data: a=2 has no b, and the row really does come back (2, NULL, NULL).
